comment: Port map for netlists/ctle_rx.cir, the 16 Gb/s receiver CTLE. The
tool turns this into port sources on the named nets, for both the
.sp sweep and the .ac characterisation the model is fitted from, so
the two see the same terminations.
z0 in = 50 ohm: the receiver input is terminated to 100 ohm
differential by RT1/RT2 in the deck, which 2 x 50 ohm ports match.
Unlike the ideal deck, the match here is NOT perfect: 250 fF of pad
and ESD capacitance per side pulls it down with frequency, which is
the point of this case.
z0 out = RD = 500 ohm: the output IS a 500 ohm load node. The port's
reference is set equal to the load the drains see so that the
measurement does not invent a load the circuit does not have. It is
not transparent either -- the node sees RD || z0 = 250 ohm while it
is measured, and the deck's header computes the output pole from
that 250 ohm rather than from RD alone.
Differential references are 2*z0: 100 ohm in, 1000 ohm out.
bias natural: each port's DC is the net's own operating-point
voltage, so no DC current flows through its z0 and the sweep
linearises about the operating point the .op above measures. Here
that matters twice over, because RD2 carries the deliberate 1%
mismatch and the two drains sit 10 mV apart (0.800 V and 0.790 V).
A port written DC 0, or both ports written to the same number, would
push current through the loads and move the bias.
passive_comment: This block is an amplifier. Its largest singular value may exceed 1
and a passivity check would fail it for working, so none is applied;
the passive companion netlists/rx_pad.cir is what exercises that
bands_comment: PROPOSED, and not yet read by the tool: moving BANDS out of
sparam_compare.py into this file is step 3a of the task, and the
second edge cannot be fixed until the first measured run reports the
model's own step. Edges are fixed numbers and are never re-derived
from the model under test; the ceiling check reports separately when
the model's ten-steps-per-period ceiling sits below an edge.

bands.name: equaliser
reason: Up to the degeneration zero at 1.9945 GHz. Below it the response
is the DC gain and a single rising asymptote, which is the part
a fitted model should reproduce most exactly.

bands.name: peaking
reason: The zero against the two output poles: 8.600 GHz and
11.368 GHz. This is the band the part is bought for -- 10 GHz is
just past the 8 GHz Nyquist of 16 Gb/s NRZ.

bands.name: below_step_ceiling
reason: To be FIXED as a number from the first measured run, as demo 5's
2.083 GHz edge was: the model's own ten-steps-per-period ceiling,
written down once and then never re-derived.

bars_comment: Empty on purpose: report-only until the per-band numbers are
measured and the bars are approved (step 5).
